info.title: Tracepad API
info.summary: Lightweight, self-hosted, OTLP-native store for LLM and agent traces.
info.description: The read API is the product's contract: the UI, the CLI and the MCP server are thin clients over exactly these endpoints, and a feature that is not here does not exist. Responses are flat snake_case JSON with RFC 3339 timestamps and opaque cursors. Every response spends a byte budget on payloads (default 51200, `?budget=` to override): a payload that does not fit is cut at a UTF-8 boundary and replaced by a truncation marker naming where the whole of it lives.

tags.name: admin
tags.description: Projects, keys, retention windows and user-data erasure

get.summary: Liveness and version, no authentication required

post.description: The canonical OTLP endpoint. Point any OpenTelemetry SDK at it with `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` and an authorization header. A 200 means the spans are committed and fsynced.

200.description: Accepted; the body is an ExportTraceServiceResponse carrying partial_success when spans were skipped

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

post.summary: OTLP ingest under the Langfuse SDK's path
post.description: The same endpoint as `/v1/traces`, at the path a Langfuse SDK sends to. Setting `LANGFUSE_HOST` to a tracepad is the whole migration.

get.summary: This endpoint map
get.description: Where an agent that has never seen this API starts: every endpoint with a one-line description, plus the link to this document. Needs no key: it says what the API is, never what is in it.

get.summary: The OpenAPI 3.1 document for this API
Version, uptime, database size and ingest counters since start
get.description: Self-diagnosis without a metrics stack. The counters are in-memory and cover this process only, which is what `counters.since` says. Row counts and counters are the asking project's own — `payloads` is absent because it cannot be attributed to one, `projects` is how many tenants share this process (naming none of them), and `size_bytes` is the whole deployment's file on disk.

200.description: What this process knows about itself

size_bytes.description: The database file plus its write-ahead log, for the whole deployment

rows.description: Row counts within the asking project, plus `projects` as a bare tenant count

counters.description: This project's ingest traffic since the process started

get.summary: List traces newest first, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: Rows carry the aggregate columns and never a payload — a listing is for choosing what to fetch. To read one trace whole, follow with `GET /api/v1/traces/{id}`; to go straight to the newest match, use `GET /api/v1/traces/last`.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's user id

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's session id

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace name

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeatable; a trace must carry every tag given

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `error` keeps traces with at least one failed observation, `ok` keeps the rest

parameters.name: min_cost
parameters.description: Keeps traces whose total cost is at least this much. A trace whose client provided no cost has none and never matches.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated subset of the row fields. An unknown name is a 400.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many rows the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap and the real number is larger

get.summary: The newest trace matching the filters, whole
get.description: The task shortcut: `?status=error&expand=io` answers "why did the last run fail" in one round trip instead of list, filter, get, and one get per observation. Takes every filter of the listing and returns exactly what `GET /api/v1/traces/{id}` returns.

404.description: Nothing matches; the message names the filters that found nothing

get.summary: One trace with its observations as a nested tree
get.description: Children are nested inside their parents, siblings ordered by start time. An observation whose parent has not arrived yet renders at the root with its `parent_observation_id` intact. Payloads ride only with `?expand=io`.

get.summary: The whole input, output and metadata of one observation
get.description: The one endpoint no byte budget applies to: it exists to be the `full` target of every truncation marker, and a budget here would recurse. A span id is unique only inside its trace, so pass `?trace_id=` when the same id appears in more than one — every truncation marker already carries the pair.

parameters.name: trace_id
parameters.description: Optional; required only when the span id is ambiguous within the project

409.description: The span id appears in more than one trace; the message lists the candidates

get.summary: List sessions by most recent activity, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: Aggregated from the traces that named a session; there is no session table. `from`/`to` bound the *traces*, half-open like the trace listing, so a session appears when any of its traces falls in the window and its totals then describe those traces. To read one session's traces, follow with `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}`.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the user id of a session's traces

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many sessions the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One session: its totals and its traces
get.description: A session is not a stored entity but the set of traces that named it. Every aggregate counts traces: `error_count` is how many of the session's traces failed, not how many spans did.

total_cost.description: Absent when no trace of the session carried a cost

get.summary: Counts, errors, cost and latency percentiles per bucket
get.description: Computed on the fly, with exact percentiles. `unit` says what a bucket counts: grouping by hour, day, environment or release counts traces, and grouping by model counts observations, because a trace has no model. Grouped by release, a trace that named none falls in the bucket with the empty key. An empty range answers with no buckets rather than with fabricated zero rows.

total_cost.description: Absent when nothing in the bucket carried a cost

post.summary: Write one score or an array of them
post.description: An array is all-or-nothing: one transaction, and one 400 naming the first invalid item. A 201 means the rows are on disk. No Content-Type is required.

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

get.summary: List scores, filtered and cursor-paginated
Fetch one score
List prompt names with where their labels point
Fetch one prompt by version, by label, or the latest
get.description: With neither `version` nor `label`, the highest version. `latest` is a virtual label meaning the same thing; there is no implicit `production`.

post.summary: Append a version to a prompt
post.description: Versions are append-only and numbered inside the write transaction, so parallel creates produce 1..N with no gaps. A name's type is fixed by its first version.

type.description: Required on the first version of a name

prompt.description: A string for a text prompt, an array of {role, content} messages for a chat one

get.summary: List a prompt's versions, newest first
get.description: Without the bodies: a version list is for picking and diffing.

get.summary: Unified diff between two versions of a prompt
get.description: A unified text patch over the pretty-printed `prompt` and `config` of the two versions — the format every consumer already reads. Empty when the two versions are identical.

put.summary: Point a label at a version
put.description: The deploy path: promote by moving `production` forward, roll back by moving it back. One row, no new version.

200.description: The version the label pointed at

get.summary: List projects
get.description: The admin token sees every project; a project key sees its own and nothing else.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `deleted` adds soft-deleted projects with their purge dates. Admin token only.

200.description: The projects the caller may see

post.summary: Create a project and its first key pair
post.description: The secret key is in this response and in no other: only its hash is stored. A name inside another project's grace window is a 409 naming the restorable one.

201.description: The project and its one-time secret

get.summary: One project with its retention windows
get.description: A soft-deleted project's own key still reaches this one, so that a caller about to restore can see what it is restoring and until when.

patch.summary: Rename a project or move its retention windows
patch.description: Renaming needs the admin token; the windows are the project's own business. `null` means keep forever. A window that shrinks is destructive: without `confirm` it answers with the preview, and it applies only when `confirm` echoes the project's name.

retention_days.description: How long a trace is kept after it arrived; null keeps it forever. Bounded because a window becomes a nanosecond cutoff, and a large enough one would overflow into the future and match every row — "forever" is null, not a big number.

raw_retention_days.description: The window for stored OTLP bodies; null follows retention_days

stats_retention_days.description: The window for the hourly statistics rollup, measured by the hour a row summarizes; null keeps it forever, which is the default. The rollup outlives the traces it summarizes, so shortening this window destroys history the trace sweep spares — it asks for the same confirmation the other two do.

200.description: The project as it is now, or the dry run of a window that shrinks

delete.summary: Soft-delete a project, restorable for seven days
delete.description: The keys stop authenticating immediately and the project vanishes from listings; the data is destroyed by the sweeper after a fixed seven-day grace. Admin token only, even for one's own project. Without `confirm` it answers with the preview.

200.description: The dry run: what deleting it would eventually destroy

202.description: Deleted, with the date the data is purged

post.summary: Undo a soft delete inside its grace window
post.description: No confirmation: it destroys nothing. Reachable with the project's own key even while deleted, so that a deployment without an admin token can still undo one.

get.summary: List a project's public keys
get.description: The secrets are not here because they are not anywhere: only their hashes are stored.

post.summary: Mint a key pair; the secret is shown once
post.description: Several active pairs are what makes rotation zero-downtime: create the new one, move the SDKs, revoke the old.

201.description: The new pair, secret included this once

delete.description: Revoking a project's last key stops its ingest, so that one is a dry run until `confirm` echoes the project's name.

200.description: The key is gone, or the dry run for the last one

delete.summary: Erase everything stored about one user
delete.description: Erases the queryable stores synchronously: the traces filed under the user id, their observations, payloads and scores. Raw OTLP bodies are not touched — they are an archive expiring on the raw retention window, which docs/retention.md documents together with what that means for an erasure request. Without `confirm` it answers with the preview; the echo here is the user id.

200.description: What was erased, or the dry run of what would be

basicKeys.description: `base64(public key:secret key)`, the shape a Langfuse SDK sends

adminToken.description: `TRACEPAD_ADMIN_TOKEN`, sent in the same header as a project key. Required for everything cross-project and for deleting a project. A server with none configured answers 403 and says so.

From.name: from
From.description: RFC 3339, inclusive. The range is half-open, so walking a timeline never reports a row twice.

Environment.name: environment
Environment.description: Exact match on the environment a trace ran in

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The opaque `next_cursor` or `prev_cursor` of a previous page

Direction.name: direction
Direction.description: Which way to page from the cursor. With no cursor, `next` is the newest page and `prev` the oldest — both ends are a direction rather than an offset. Rows come back newest first either way

Count.name: count
Count.description: Adds `total` and `total_capped`: how many rows the filters match, counted up to 1000. Off by default, because the count changes with the filters and not with the page

Search.name: q
Search.description: Full-text search over one field of one observation — input, output, metadata, name or status message — or over the trace name. Words (all must occur), `"quoted phrases"`, `prefix*`. Words, not substrings: `error` does not find `errors`, `err*` finds both. Case and diacritics are folded, identifiers split on punctuation, and only the first 64 KiB of each payload is indexed. A `q` with no word in it is a 400

Release.name: release
Release.description: Exact match on the deployment the trace ran in, from `langfuse.release` or the resource's `service.version`

Version.name: version
Version.description: Exact match on the version of the trace's own logic, from `langfuse.version`

ObservationType.name: type
ObservationType.description: Keeps traces with at least one observation of this kind. Exact: `generation` does not match `embedding`. A value outside the list is a 400

Prompt.name: prompt
Prompt.description: `name` or `name@version`: keeps traces with at least one observation that ran this prompt, at any version or at that one. A version is a run of digits after the last `@` with a name in front of it; every other string is a name, `@` included — `@acme/support`, `team@acme/answer`, `name@latest` and `svc@-1` all filter as names. A label is not a version

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description: `io` inlines each observation's input, output and metadata, each cut to an equal share of the remaining budget with a truncation marker naming the rest

Budget.name: budget
Budget.description: Byte budget for the payloads of this response; the structure is never truncated

Confirm.name: confirm
Confirm.description: The name of the project — or the id of the user — being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with a preview; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

BadRequest.description: The request cannot mean what it says: an unknown query parameter, a malformed value, a limit out of range

Unauthorized.description: The credentials do not resolve to a project

NotFound.description: No such thing in this project

Forbidden.description: The credentials are good but do not reach this far: cross-project administration needs the admin token

Conflict.description: The stored state already answers differently: a name that is taken, a project that is already deleted

Error.description: The one error shape the whole surface uses

TraceRow.description: A trace as it appears in a listing: aggregates only, never a payload. A field the trace never carried is absent rather than empty.

release.description: The deployment the trace ran in, from `langfuse.release` or the resource's `service.version`

version.description: The version of the trace's own logic, from `langfuse.version`

timestamp.description: When the earliest observation of the trace started

total_cost.description: Summed over the observations whose client provided cost; absent when none did

ttft_ms.description: The wait before the first token: the earliest completion start among the trace's observations, minus the trace's own start. Absent when no observation carried one, and negative when a client's completion start precedes its span

Match.description: Where the search hit, present only with `?q=`: the observation and field with the best score among the trace's hits, and a window of the text around the first term. Hits are not marked up — a client that highlights folds the query terms the way the tokenizer does.

observation_id.description: The observation that matched; null when the trace's own name did

snippet.description: At most 160 characters, cut on word boundaries

SessionRow.description: The roll-up over the traces of one session. Every number counts traces, not observations: `error_count` is how many of the session's traces failed.

id.description: The session id, as the application set it

total_cost.description: Summed over the traces that carried a cost; absent when none did

Observation.description: One span. `children` holds the spans that named it as their parent and is absent for a leaf.

parent_observation_id.description: The observation this one ran under, whenever it named one. Nested children carry it too; an observation whose parent is not in this trace renders at the root and still carries it.

type.description: What kind of step this was. A span whose client named no type is classified: a model attribute makes it a generation, a zero-duration childless span an event, anything else a span

completion_start_time.description: When the first token came back, as the client reported it — stored uncorrected, so it may precede `start_time`

ttft_ms.description: `completion_start_time` minus `start_time`; absent when either is missing

input_bytes.description: The uncompressed size of `input`, present whether or not the payload itself is inlined

PromptLink.description: The prompt the client said this observation ran. Recorded as sent and resolved against no registry — the store may not manage this prompt at all, and a label that points at nothing is still a label. Absent when the client named none.

version.description: Null when the client named a prompt without a whole-number version

Expansion.description: Present only when `?expand=io` was refused: a trace with more payloads than the budget can carry markers for gets none of them and this instead. Nothing is unreachable — the tree lists every observation id — and `budget_needed` is what to retry `?budget=` with.

payloads.description: How many payloads the trace holds.

budget_needed.description: The budget that would carry a marker for each of them. Never clamped to the maximum, so it may exceed what `?budget=` accepts.

retryable.description: Whether `budget_needed` is a budget this server would accept. False means no budget can carry this many markers — read the payloads one at a time instead.

Truncation.description: A payload too large for this response's budget. `full` is the URL that returns it whole; `trace_id` and `observation_id` are the same target for a consumer that speaks tools rather than URLs.

size.description: The payload's full size in bytes

preview.description: A prefix of the payload, cut on a UTF-8 boundary

ScoreInput.description: One judgement. A score needs a trace or a session, and either a `value` or a `string_value`.

id.description: Generated when absent; writing the same id again replaces the score

data_type.description: Inferred when absent: a `value` makes it numeric, a `string_value` makes it text

timestamp.description: Event time; defaults to receive time

prompt.description: Stored and returned verbatim; interpolation is the client's job

Project.description: A project with its retention windows. `deleted_at` and `purge_at` are present only while a soft delete is inside its grace window.

retention_days.description: null means the data is kept forever, which is the default

stats_retention_days.description: The window for the statistics rollup, which outlives the traces it summarizes; null means it is kept forever, which is the default

purge_at.description: When the sweeper destroys the data; seven days after the delete, and not configurable

NewKey.description: A freshly minted key pair. The secret appears here and nowhere else, ever.

DryRun.description: What a destructive request would do, which is what it does until it is confirmed

oldest.description: Arrival of the oldest affected row; absent when nothing is affected

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

Deletion.description: What a confirmed destructive request actually removed
